facts.text: The Texas Panhandle spans 25,823.89 square miles, almost the size of West Virginia, and is bordered by New Mexico to the west and Oklahoma to the north and east.
The 103rd meridian west became the Panhandle’s northern border when the Compromise of 1850 removed Texas territory north of that line.
Charles Goodnight founded the JA Ranch in 1876, the first cattle ranch in the Panhandle, and it grew into one of the world’s largest open‑range operations.
The Panhandle’s broad mesa and expansive grassland prairies define its landscape, with the Llano Estacado’s flat surface breaking at the Canadian River.
Native American tribes such as the Apache and Comanche originally inhabited the Panhandle before Spanish explorers, Texas Rangers, and Buffalo Soldiers arrived.
The Panhandle’s history is preserved in museums like the Panhandle‑Plains Historical Museum, Texas’ largest history museum, and the Charles and Mary Ann Goodnight Ranch State Historic Site.
